title: Conditional small-set expansion bound
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ take only the values $0$ and $1$, and suppose its uniform mean is $\alpha>0$. Draw $(X,Y)$ by choosing $X$ uniformly from the sign cube and then independently, in each coordinate, keeping its sign with probability $2/3$ and flipping it with probability $1/3$. Then $\mathbb P(f(X)=f(Y)=1)/\alpha\le\sqrt{\alpha}$.
replaced:
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ take only the values $0$ and $1$,
and let its uniform mean be $\alpha>0$. If $(X,Y)$ is drawn by choosing $X$ uniformly
and then independently flipping each coordinate of $X$ with probability $1/3$, then the
probability that $f(X)=f(Y)=1$, divided by $\alpha$, is at most $\sqrt{\alpha}$.
